narration: This week's parsha is Parshas Lech Lecha!
Hashem spoke to Avram: Lech lecha! Leave your land, your birthplace and your father's house, and go to the land that I will show you.
It will be good for you, said Hashem. There I will make you a great nation, and I will bless you, and everyone will know your name.
So Avram set out, with his wife Sarai and his nephew Lot.
With them came all the people Avram and Sarai had taught about Hashem in Charan.
They traveled all the way to the land of Canaan, and wherever Avram went, he built a mizbe'ach and called out in the name of Hashem.
Then there was a famine in the land, so Avram and Sarai went down to Mitzrayim.
Pharaoh's men took Sarai to the palace. But Hashem protected her, and struck Pharaoh's house with great plagues,
until Pharaoh sent Avram and Sarai away, with many gifts.
Avram and Lot both had so many sheep and cattle that there wasn't room for everyone.
Lot's shepherds were letting their animals eat in other people's fields, and Avram's shepherds told them: that's stealing!
So Avram said to Lot: let's not fight, we are family. You choose where to go.
Lot looked at the green valley near Sedom, and went to live there, even though the people of Sedom were very wicked.
Then four mighty kings went to war against five kings, and they captured Lot.
When Avram heard, he went after them. Chazal say he took only his loyal servant Eliezer.
In the middle of the night, they chased the kings away, and rescued Lot and all the captives!
Malki-tzedek, king of Shalem, came out to greet Avram with bread and wine. Rashi tells us he was Shem, the son of Noach!
The king of Sedom wanted to give Avram a big reward. But Avram said: I won't take even a thread or a shoelace. Hashem is the One who makes me rich.
Avram still had no children. So Hashem took him outside and said: look up at the sky, and count the stars, if you can.
So many will your children be! And Avram believed in Hashem.
Sarai still had no children, so she gave Avram her maidservant Hagar as a wife, and Hagar had a son, Yishmael.
When Avram was ninety-nine years old, Hashem changed his name. He added the letter hei, and Avram became Avraham, father of many nations. And Sarai became Sarah.
Hashem gave Avraham the mitzvah of bris milah, a sign of the covenant between Hashem and his children forever.
And Hashem made a wonderful promise: Sarah will have a son, and you will call him Yitzchak!
Avraham fell on his face and rejoiced.
But how will it happen? That's a story for next week!
Good Shabbos!
